sentences.zh: 这里是百分之九十九隐形。

sentences.en: This summer, the governors of New Mexico and Colorado got into a fight on Twitter.
sentences.zh: 今年夏天，新墨西哥州和科罗拉多州的州长在推特上吵了一架。

sentences.en: Words were had, umbrage was taken.
But the fight wasn't over tax incentives or highway funding or water rights.
sentences.zh: 但这场争论不是为了税收优惠、高速公路资金或水权。

sentences.en: Instead, it all boiled down to this.
sentences.zh: 相反，这一切都归结于一件事。

sentences.en: Colorado's governor had the gall to insult New Mexico's pride and joy.
sentences.zh: 科罗拉多州长竟然敢侮辱新墨西哥州的骄傲与挚爱。

sentences.en: The latest war of words comes after Colorado's governor made some insulting comments about our chili.
sentences.zh: 在这场最新骂战爆发前，科罗拉多州长对我们的辣椒发表了一些侮辱性言论。

sentences.en: Colorado's governor, Jared Polis, is claiming the chili in Pueblo is better than ours.
sentences.zh: 科罗拉多州长贾雷德·波利斯声称普韦布洛的辣椒比我们的更好。

sentences.en: Naturally, New Mexico's governor had no choice but to respond in kind.
sentences.zh: 理所当然地，新墨西哥州长别无选择，只能以其人之道还治其人之身。

sentences.en: This morning, Governor Michelle Lujan Grisham defended our precious crop on Twitter, saying, quote,
sentences.zh: 今天早上，州长米歇尔·卢汉·格里沙姆在推特上捍卫了我们珍贵的农作物，并引用了一句话：

sentences.en: If Pueblo chili were any good, it would have been on national shelves before now.
sentences.zh: 如果普韦布洛辣椒真有什么过人之处，早就摆上全国各地的货架了。

sentences.en: In New Mexico, chili peppers are everywhere.
sentences.zh: 在新墨西哥州，辣椒随处可见。

sentences.en: Ristras of dried chilies hang from every doorway.
sentences.zh: 一串串风干的红辣椒挂在每个门口。

sentences.en: They are prominently featured on license plates.
sentences.zh: 车牌上也能看到它们的显眼标志。

sentences.en: Chili pepper cheeseburgers are part of the standard menu at McDonald's.
sentences.zh: 辣椒芝士汉堡是麦当劳的标准菜单之一。

sentences.en: I can report they are not very good.
sentences.zh: 我可以汇报一下，它们其实不怎么好吃。

sentences.en: And New Mexico remains the only state in the union with an official state question.
sentences.zh: 而且新墨西哥州依然是全美唯一一个拥有官方州立问题的州。

sentences.en: It's chili season right now in New Mexico, which means that the state's chili pepper pride is ramped up to the next level.
sentences.zh: 现在正是新墨西哥州的辣椒季，这意味着该州对辣椒的自豪感高涨到了极点。

sentences.en: That's reporter Rose Eveleth, host of the Flash Forward podcaSt.
sentences.zh: 说话的是《前瞻》播客的主持人、记者罗斯·埃夫莱斯。

sentences.en: There are chili-scented candles for sale.
sentences.zh: 市面上有辣椒香味的蜡烛在售。

sentences.en: The roads are dotted with big white signs that say, fresh chili, this way.
sentences.zh: 道路两旁点缀着醒目的大白牌子，上面写着：新鲜辣椒，由此进。

sentences.en: And every parking lot seems to have a roaster going, tumbling green and red chili peppers over a fire.
sentences.zh: 每个停车场似乎都有人在转动烘烤机，让红绿辣椒在火上翻滚。

sentences.en: And in September 2019, on an incredibly windy day in Socorro, the New Mexico Chili Association hosted the first-ever New Mexico Chili Taste-Off.
sentences.zh: 2019年9月，在索科罗一个风大得惊人的日子里，新墨西哥州辣椒协会举办了史上首届新墨西哥州辣椒盲品大赛。

sentences.en: And when I asked farmers at the Chili Taste-Off about the rivalry with Colorado, they basically just laughed.
sentences.zh: 当我在辣椒盲品大赛上问起农户们与科罗拉多州的竞争时，他们基本上都笑了。
不，科罗拉多吓不倒我们。

sentences.en: She asked us if we were worried about Colorado chili.
sentences.zh: 她问我们是否担心科罗拉多辣椒。

sentences.en: No, if I want to go to Colorado for something, it won't be for chili.
sentences.zh: 不，如果我要为了什么事去科罗拉多，那绝对不是为了辣椒。
但也说不定连滑雪都不会去。

sentences.en: Amidst all this Colorado trash-talking, the organizers of the Chili Taste-Off also crowned the Chili Queen of New Mexico.
sentences.zh: 在科罗拉多人的各种大放厥词中，辣椒盲品大赛的组织者还加冕了新墨西哥州辣椒女王。

sentences.en: June Rutherford, your royal chili highness, is 95 years old.
sentences.zh: 琼·拉瑟福德，您这位辣椒王室殿下已经95岁高龄了。

sentences.en: June has been in the business since she was a little girl, when her father carried her around in the fields in a pepper sack.
sentences.zh: 琼从小就在这行里干活，那时她父亲用一个装辣椒的麻袋把她背在田间地头。

sentences.en: There's even a chili pepper variety named after her, the Miss Junie.
sentences.zh: 甚至还有一个以她名字命名的辣椒品种，叫“琼小姐”。

sentences.en: And she wasn't going to let a little wind stop her from talking up New Mexico Chili.
sentences.zh: 一点微风可阻挡不了她为新墨西哥州辣椒大加赞赏。

sentences.en: Our chili has a better taste than anywhere else.
sentences.zh: 我们的辣椒比其他任何地方的都好吃。

sentences.en: Texas, Arizona, California, and even Colorado can't beat us.
sentences.zh: 得克萨斯、亚利桑那、加利福尼亚，甚至科罗拉多都打败不了我们。

sentences.en: We have something that nobody's got.
sentences.zh: 我们拥有别人没有的东西。

sentences.en: There's no secret ingredient to New Mexico's chili peppers, unless you count tradition.
sentences.zh: 新墨西哥辣椒没有什么秘方，除非你把传统也算上。

sentences.en: New Mexicans like June have been growing their own varieties for over 100 years,
sentences.zh: 像琼这样的新墨西哥人培育自己的品种已经有一百多年了，

sentences.en: mostly on small family farms that will remain dedicated to this one beloved crop for generations.
sentences.zh: 大多是在家族小农场里，他们世世代代都专注于这一种挚爱的农作物。

sentences.en: But despite these growers' pride in their peppers, all is not well in Miss Junie's kingdom.
sentences.zh: 但尽管这些种植者为自己的辣椒感到自豪，琼小姐的王国里并非一帆风顺。

sentences.en: New Mexico's chili may be the best in the world.
sentences.zh: 新墨西哥州的辣椒可能是世界上最好的。

sentences.en: But for a while now, the chili business has been in trouble.
sentences.zh: 但一段时间以来，辣椒产业一直陷入困境。

sentences.en: New Mexico chili farmers have a problem, one that might soon force them to choose between tradition and technology.
sentences.zh: 新墨西哥州的辣椒农遇到了一个问题，这个问题可能很快会迫使他们在传统与技术之间做出选择。

sentences.en: When I started reporting this story, everybody told me I had to talk to a guy named Glenn Duggins.
sentences.zh: 当我开始报道这个故事时，所有人都告诉我必须去和一个叫格伦·达金斯的人谈谈。

sentences.en: They told me that Glenn was a great, cheery, friendly guy.
sentences.zh: 他们告诉我格伦是个很棒、很开朗、很友善的人。

sentences.en: But when I first called him about chili, and I asked,
sentences.zh: 但当我第一次打电话跟他聊辣椒时，我问：

sentences.en: Do you ever get nostalgic about the old chili days?
sentences.zh: 你对过去的辣椒日子有过怀念吗？

sentences.en: We stayed drunk most of the time.
sentences.zh: 我们大部分时间都喝得醉醺醺的。

sentences.en: I mean, we had a good time at it.
sentences.zh: 我是说，我们当时过得很开心。

sentences.en: It's not near as fun anymore.
sentences.zh: 现在可一点意思也没有了。

sentences.en: Glenn runs a chili farm called Five Star Chili in Socorro, New Mexico.
sentences.zh: 格伦在新墨西哥州索科罗经营着一家名为“五星辣椒”的辣椒农场。

sentences.en: And he says that every year, things get a little more bleak for the business.
sentences.zh: 他说，随着一年过去，这个行业的生意变得越来越暗淡。

sentences.en: It's not that nobody wants to buy chili.
sentences.zh: 并不是没有人想买辣椒。

sentences.en: Nationwide demand for chili peppers is at an all-time high.
sentences.zh: 全国对辣椒的需求量达到了历史最高水平。

sentences.en: And yet, the economics of being a chili farmer, they're just not working out.
sentences.zh: 然而，做辣椒农的经济效益就是行不通。

sentences.en: It's like the perfect storm came together.
sentences.zh: 这就像是各种不利因素汇聚到了一起。
我们遇到了糟糕的天气。

sentences.en: To make matters worse, chili grown in Mexico is often trucked over the border.
sentences.zh: 更糟糕的是，墨西哥种植的辣椒经常被卡车运过边境。

sentences.en: Labeled as New Mexico chili and sold for far cheaper than the farmers in the state can compete with.
sentences.zh: 贴上新墨西哥辣椒的标签出售，价格比州内农户的成本低得多，根本无法竞争。

sentences.en: But Glenn says that there's one thing in particular that has him and other chili farmers especially worried.
sentences.zh: 但格伦说，有一件事特别让他和其他辣椒农感到担忧。

sentences.en: Chili farmers are used to bad weather, to competition, to all that other stuff.
sentences.zh: 辣椒农已经习惯了恶劣天气、竞争以及所有这些其他的事情。

sentences.en: But now, even if they had perfect weather, a perfect crop of chilies, and no competition at all, they'd still have a problem.
sentences.zh: 但现在，即使他们拥有完美的天气、完美的辣椒收成，而且完全没有任何竞争，他们依然会有麻烦。

sentences.en: There just aren't enough workers to pick the peppers.
sentences.zh: 根本没有足够的工人来采摘辣椒。

sentences.en: We hire everybody that comes up.
sentences.zh: 我们雇佣所有来应聘的人。

sentences.en: When I visited Glenn's farm, he had eight workers out in the field picking chilies.
sentences.zh: 我参观格伦的农场时，地里只有八个工人在摘辣椒。

sentences.en: He says on a good year, in the past, he would have had 30.
sentences.zh: 他说过去在丰收年，他会有30个工人。

sentences.en: Somehow, they would go to one ranch house, work a few days for them.
sentences.zh: 不知怎么的，他们会去一个农庄，在那里干几天活。

sentences.en: They would feed them, take care of them, and this and that, and go to the next ranch house.
sentences.zh: 农场主会管他们饭，照顾他们，诸如此类，然后再去下一个农庄。

sentences.en: And they would eventually get here.

sentences.zh: 这种情况已经好多年没发生了。

sentences.en: Ten years ago, he used to wake up in the morning, at the start of chili season,
sentences.zh: 十年前，在辣椒季刚开始的早晨，他醒来时，

sentences.en: and have the 30 guys he needed just standing in his driveway.
sentences.zh: 他需要的30个小伙子就直接站在他的车道上。

sentences.en: Like at your door, they just knock on your door.
sentences.zh: 就像来到你门前，直接敲你的门。

sentences.en: Yeah, they know where to go.
And it's not just the chili industry.
Farms across the United States are reporting shortages of labor.
sentences.zh: 全美各地的农场都在报告劳动力短缺。

sentences.en: Since 2002, the number of immigrants coming to the United States to work in agriculture has dropped by 75%.
sentences.zh: 自2002年以来，来美国从事农业工作的移民数量下降了75%。

sentences.en: In California, one survey found that 56% of farmers were unable to hire enough workers.
sentences.zh: 在加利福尼亚州，一项调查发现56%的农场主无法雇到足够的工人。

sentences.en: The number of people immigrating to the U.S.
sentences.zh: 移居美国从事农业劳动的总人数

sentences.en: for farm labor has actually been going down since 2008,
sentences.zh: 实际上自2008年以来一直在下降，

sentences.en: like when the economy crashed here.
sentences.zh: 就像当年这里经济崩溃的时候一样。

sentences.en: That's Sarah Tabor, a crop scientist based in Fayetteville, North Carolina.
sentences.zh: 说话的是萨拉·泰伯，一位常驻北卡罗来纳州费耶特ville的农作物科学家。

sentences.en: And she says the Great Recession scrambled the familiar labor paradigm,
sentences.zh: 她说，大萧条打破了人们熟悉的劳动力模式，

sentences.en: in which migrant workers would arrive in the U.S.
sentences.zh: 即外来务工人员会来到美国

sentences.en: A lot of folks were like, wait, I can actually do better for myself just staying home in Mexico.
sentences.zh: 很多人觉得，等等，我留在墨西哥老家其实能过得更好。

sentences.en: Increasingly, potential foreign workers are staying put in their home countries to work in places like call centers.
sentences.zh: 越来越多的潜在外国工人选择留在祖国，去呼叫中心之类的地方工作。

sentences.en: And Sarah points out that the children of immigrants who came to the U.S.
sentences.zh: 萨拉指出，那些来到美国并从事农业的移民的子女，
因此，那些曾经来美国从事农业劳动的群体正在变老。

sentences.en: So the folks who already came to the U.S.
sentences.zh: 而他们的孩子并不打算从事这一行。

sentences.en: for farm labor, they're getting older.
sentences.zh: 他们来这里是为了过上更好的生活。

sentences.en: And their kids are not going into that.
sentences.zh: 他们会对孩子们说，求求你们，千万别去摘辣椒。

sentences.en: They're here to make their lives better.
sentences.zh: 甚至并不是因为这份工作薪水不高。

sentences.en: And they're like, please, kids, don't go into picking chilies.
It's not even that this work doesn't pay well.
sentences.zh: 新墨西哥州辣椒田的农场工人挣的钱可以达到该州最低工资的两倍。
他们摘辣椒赚到的钱，几乎是在辣椒餐厅打工的两倍。

sentences.en: Farm laborers in New Mexico's chili fields can make double the state's minimum wage.
They can make nearly twice as much picking chili as they could working at a Chili's restaurant.
sentences.zh: 部分原因在于，即使和其他农作物相比，采摘辣椒也是一项极其折磨人的工作。

sentences.en: But they still don't want to do it.
sentences.zh: 辣椒植株长得很低，贴近地面，

sentences.en: In part because picking chili peppers can be especially grueling work, even compared to other crops.
sentences.zh: 而且辣椒本身通常紧挨着茎部，深深地隐藏在灌木丛中。

sentences.en: Chili plants grow low to the ground,
sentences.zh: 所以工人们必须在炎热的太阳下弯腰驼背才能摘到它们。

sentences.en: and the chilies themselves often sit close to the stem, nestled deep inside the bush.
sentences.zh: 这一切还得戴着手套，以保护双手免受辣椒特征性辣味的油脂伤害。

sentences.en: So workers have to hunch over in the hot sun to get them.
sentences.zh: 青辣椒——也就是格伦和许多其他新墨西哥辣椒农依赖的品种——

sentences.en: All this while wearing gloves to protect their hands from the oils that give chilies their characteristic heat.
And green chili peppers, the kind Glenn and a lot of other New Mexico chili farmers rely on,
sentences.zh: 青辣椒只是还没熟透的红辣椒，这意味着它们里面的种子还没有准备好发芽。
植物不想交出果实，所以它的茎部不经一番拉锯战是绝不会松手的。

sentences.en: Green chilies are just unripe red chilies, which means that the seeds inside of them aren't ready to germinate yet.
sentences.zh: 我们每年都会雇人，比如需要工作的当地公民，他们说，哦，我能干这个，结果到了中午就辞职了。

sentences.en: The plant doesn't want to give its fruits up, so its stems won't let go without a fight.
And we hire people every year, like citizens here that need a job and, oh, I can do that, and they quit by noon.

sentences.zh: 他们不想弯腰驼背地摘辣椒或者拔野草。

sentences.en: They don't want to stoop over and pick chili or whole weeds.
sentences.zh: 我是说，我自己也不会去干。

sentences.en: I mean, I'm not going to do it.
sentences.zh: 为了维持生存，像格伦这样的小型家族农场每年都在减少辣椒的种植面积，
转而种植其他对劳动力需求较少的农作物。

sentences.en: In order to stay afloat, small family farms like Glenn's have been planting less and less chili every year
sentences.zh: 1997年，新墨西哥州的辣椒种植面积超过了3万英亩。

sentences.en: in favor of other less labor-intensive crops.
sentences.zh: 去年，这一数字仅剩下8400英亩。

sentences.en: In 1997, New Mexico chili farmers planted over 30,000 acres.
sentences.zh: 现在，一些年轻的农场主正选择根本不种辣椒。
（注：根据输入的键范围补齐到149）

sentences.en: And now, some younger farmers are opting not to plant chili at all.
sentences.zh: （注：根据输入的键范围补齐到149）

sentences.en: As Glenn showed me around his farm, he pointed out into the distance,
sentences.zh: 当格伦带我参观他的农场时，他指向远方，

sentences.en: where his son was driving a tractor, raking up hay.
sentences.zh: 他的儿子正开着拖拉机在收割牧草。

sentences.en: Are you going to take over after you retire?
I think, but he won't do chili, I bet.
sentences.zh: 我想会的，但我敢说他不会种辣椒。

sentences.en: He sees what I go through.
I mean, what we have, we made years ago.
sentences.zh: 我是说，我们现在拥有的，是多年前创造的。

sentences.en: We haven't done anything in the last six, eight years.
sentences.zh: 在过去六、八年里，我们什么都没做。

sentences.en: Do you think it'll ever get back to that?
sentences.zh: 你觉得以后还能恢复到以前那样吗？

sentences.en: Glenn genuinely doesn't know the answer to that question,
sentences.zh: 格伦其实并不知道这个问题的答案，

sentences.en: nor do a lot of other chili farmers.
sentences.zh: 许多其他辣椒种植户也不知道。

sentences.en: But if you've been paying attention to almost every other industry,
sentences.zh: 但如果你一直在关注其他几乎所有行业，

sentences.en: why can't Glenn just get a machine to pick his peppers?
sentences.zh: 为什么格伦就不能用机器来采摘辣椒呢？

sentences.en: After all, it wouldn't be the first time a machine has replaced human hands in the field.
sentences.zh: 毕竟，这并非田间地头第一次用机器取代人手。

sentences.en: Especially, as Sarah Tabor points out,
sentences.zh: 正如萨拉·塔博尔（Sarah Tabor）所指出的，

sentences.en: in a country with abundant land and scarce labor.
sentences.zh: 尤其是在一个土地资源丰富而劳动力匮乏的国家。
在美国，如果你是个白人，

sentences.en: if you are a white person in the United States,
And as a result, you could get way more land
sentences.zh: 因此，你能轻松获得的土地，

sentences.en: than you could actually work yourself pretty easily.
sentences.zh: 往往远超你一个人实际能耕种的极限。

sentences.en: So then what do you do with it?
sentences.zh: 那该拿这些土地怎么办呢？

sentences.en: In the South, landowners cultivated more land than they could on their own
sentences.zh: 在南方，土地所有者通过奴役劳动力，
耕种了超出自身能力的广阔土地。

sentences.en: the same landowners increasingly rented their land out
sentences.zh: 这些地主转而以苛刻的条件，

sentences.en: and, in the North, to tenant farmers,
sentences.zh: 在北方则租给农场佃户，

sentences.en: who would harvest things like grain.
sentences.zh: 让他们去收割谷物之类的作物。

sentences.en: So, like, grain used to be really, really super labor-intensive.
sentences.zh: 所以，以前谷物种植是非常非常需要大量人工的。

sentences.en: You had to cut it by hand, you had to dry it, stack it,
sentences.zh: 你得靠手去割、去晾晒、去码垛、

sentences.en: thresh it, you know, all that stuff that was all done by hand.
sentences.zh: 去脱粒，你懂的，这些全都要手工完成。

sentences.en: commercial production began on a combine harvester,
sentences.zh: 联合收割机开始投入商业生产，

sentences.en: a machine that could do it all at once.
sentences.zh: 这是一种能一步到位完成所有工序的机器。

sentences.en: That's why they call it a combine.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么它们被称为联合收割机（Combine）。
联合收割机的出现让地主们
